description: The CrossModal Study is an EEG dataset investigating attentional preparation and target discrimination across auditory and visual modalities. Participants received cues to prepare for targets in either auditory or visual domains, with a 3-second preparation interval featuring frequency-tagged visual stimuli (36 Hz) and amplitude-modulated auditory stimuli (40 Hz). The dataset captures neural oscillations, particularly alpha activity, during cross-modal attention and target preparation tasks with systematic manipulation of cue validity and distractor presence.
methods_description: EEG data were recorded during a cross-modal target discrimination task with six experimental conditions combining auditory/visual cues and targets with varying distractor presence. Participants performed 28 blocks of trials following practice, with targets requiring discrimination via keyboard response. An additional EOG channel monitored eye activity. Data were acquired at Birmingham University, UK, and processed using FieldTrip (version 20251106) for BIDS conversion.
